patch_description:
The current program uses 34 restarts × 5350 sequential single-candidate annealing moves, with initial scale 0.125, final scale 0.0075, and an exponentially decaying temperature. This is expensive because every proposal recomputes all 165 triangle areas separately, and late annealing can still accept a weaker strict bottleneck.

The replacement uses vectorized differential-evolution islands: 3 islands of 144 configurations for 420 generations, followed by a 520-round active-constraint batch polish with 128 proposals per round. All geometry is evaluated directly in affine simplex coordinates, where determinant magnitude equals normalized triangle area. Early generations use a lower-tail score to balance several nearly active triangles; the final 45% switches to lexicographic selection dominated by the raw minimum area, preventing soft-tail improvements from sacrificing the true bottleneck. Active-set polishing perturbs points incident to the smallest 18 constraints, with decreasing scales from 0.020 to 0.00016.
